correctness.rationale: For each positive parameter pair, the BV Jordan step-measure decomposition reduces the operator norm exactly to a supremum of two explicit one-jump output variations. Direct integration yields A(s), B(s); their differentiated integral brackets are strictly decreasing with opposite endpoint signs, furnishing unique interior maxima. Substitution yields gains 1-(1-s)^beta and 1-t^alpha, equality forces the derivative measure to a single jump. The noncommuting (1,2) example uses the exact rational-log inequality (2/3)log(3)-2/9>1/2. The packaged deterministic checker validates formula samples and signed-step numerics, not the universal proof.

This addresses whether alternating causal/anticausal averaging improves BV stability, beyond routine one-sided Hardy bounds.
